label: HEALING

cover.headline: Staying friends with an ex: *when it works*

points.heading: Am I hoping for more?
points.body: If you’re secretly hoping to get back together, friendship can keep you stuck.
points.panel: “Would I be okay seeing him with someone new?”

points.heading: Has enough time passed?
points.body: Space first usually makes friendship possible later.
points.panel: Try a few months of distance before deciding.

points.heading: Does it help me heal?
points.body: Notice how you feel after you talk.
points.panel: “Do I feel lighter or heavier after we speak?”

points.heading: Is it mutual and respectful?
points.body: Friendship only works if both people want the same thing.

points.heading: It’s okay to say no
points.body: Not every ex needs to become a friend.
points.panel: “I wish you well, but I need distance.”

close.save: Save this for when you’re deciding.

caption:
“Let’s stay friends” sounds kind, but it isn’t always the right choice, at least not right away.

These five honest questions help you decide whether a friendship with your ex would help you heal or keep you stuck. Either answer is okay, and you can change your mind later.

Save this for when you’re deciding, and follow @roundabloom for more gentle steps.
